Q6.question: What contextual factors (e.g., academic stress, social support systems) should an expert review consider when interpreting a low screening risk score?
Q6.answer: When interpreting a low screening risk score, experts should consider contextual factors that may lead to symptom masking or under-reporting. For instance, individuals may report somatic symptoms or mask depressive symptoms to avoid mental health stigma, which can lead to under-detection of issues. Furthermore, a comprehensive review should look beyond symptoms to assess indicators of well-being, positive mental health, life satisfaction, school belonging, and social determinants of mental health. Screening measures can also gather information on these strengths alongside any reported difficulties. Considering both the student's strengths and symptoms provides a more complete picture of their mental health status.
